collection.description: A child in a grass crown demands to rule for a day: let the child govern, or have the Chief explain leadership.

question.name: The Child Who Claimed to Be Chief
question.text: A child of {@city} appears before {@tribal_chief} wearing a crown of woven grass and declares that the village has been governed incorrectly. The child demands the right to rule for one day. {@Chief} considers the challenge while the gathered villagers struggle not to laugh.

choices.label: Let the child govern for one day under {@chief}'s supervision.
Have {@chief} explain the responsibilities of leadership.

a1.text: The child decrees that everyone must play. {@Chief} asks who will gather supper. After a hungry afternoon, the young ruler reluctantly withdraws the decree.

a2.text:
The child asks why supplies are carried back and forth so often. {@Chief} allows the farmers to test a better arrangement.
{@Chief} publicly praises the child's observation.

a3.text:
The child demands a feast fit for a ruler. {@Chief} places the child in charge of gathering and preparing it.
The child learns what such orders cost.

a4.text: Two quarrelling adults are ordered to share their tools. The solution works, much to {@chief}'s delight and the adults' embarrassment.

b1.text: {@Chief} invites the child to help an exhausted farmer. By sunset the child admits that leadership is harder than wearing a crown.

b2.text: The child challenges {@chief} to a public debate and makes a surprisingly clever argument. {@Chief} graciously acknowledges it, whereupon the child forgets the subject entirely.

b3.text: The child happily withdraws the challenge in favor of hide-and-seek. {@Chief} solemnly accepts the abdication and returns to governing.
